review_subject: FRANK/ClayCode assumption that declarative architecture relations can share a typed semantic IR with executable ClayCode without allowing representation to become authority or allowing ambiguous legacy syntax to choose semantics silently

independent_inputs.finding: all three residual legacy rules admit multiple plausible ASTs; registry-gated n-ary IR rejects unknown relations and wrong arities 10000/10000 each
ambiguous expression grammars require explicit precedence/associativity; grammar mechanics do not by themselves establish domain intent
declarative IR can use explicit operation definitions, traits and constraints rather than unconstrained free-form operator vocabulary

counterhypotheses_tested: operator precedence alone can safely choose the intended meaning of the three remaining legacy rules
arbitrary identifiers as relations are safe because later checking can repair ambiguity
FRANK architectural agreement is sufficient evidence for a ClayCode source rewrite
refinement: The safest current BASE interpretation is a three-way separation: executable expression operators with explicit precedence/associativity; typed declarative PredicateIR/ConstraintIR with declared relation signatures; and a fail-closed semantic-freeze gate for legacy clauses whose source text admits multiple materially different ASTs. FRANK requirements remain input to the freeze decision, not independent proof and not effect authority.
not_supported: the exact intended AST of any of the three ambiguous legacy lines
automatic rewrite of current G9 source
any expansion of model or FRANK execution authority
next_falsifier: Locate authoritative prior IR/parser lineage for the three legacy clauses or explicitly freeze their intended typed IR, then run them through the production parser/canonicalizer/type-effect checker and roundtrip semantic-hash tests on the Ubuntu target.
